Nitpick comments: 2
packages/ai-gemini/tests/embedding-adapter.test.ts: 2
`86-94`: ** Trivial** · **Maintainability & Code Quality** · **Quick win** **Make the batching test fail when batches run concurrently.** The mock resolves every `embedContent` call immediately. A version that starts all three batches with `Promise.all` would still pass. The assertions check the call count, batch sizes, result length, and vector order. None of them checks whether calls overlap. Hold the first call open with a deferred promise. Then assert that only one call exists before you release it.
Suggested mock change
```diff + let releaseFirstBatch: () => void = () => {} + let firstBatchCalled = false spy.mockImplementation(({ contents }) => { const items = Array.isArray(contents) ? contents : [contents] if (items.length > 100) { return Promise.reject(new Error('at most 100 requests per batch')) } - return Promise.resolve( - mockResponse(items.map((text) => [Number(String(text).slice(1))])), - ) + const response = mockResponse( + items.map((text) => [Number(String(text).slice(1))]), + ) + if (!firstBatchCalled) { + firstBatchCalled = true + return new Promise((resolve) => { + releaseFirstBatch = () => resolve(response) + }) + } + return Promise.resolve(response) }) ```
In the test, start `createEmbeddings` without awaiting it. Flush pending microtasks, for example with `await new Promise((resolve) => setTimeout(resolve, 0))`. Assert that `spy.mock.calls.length` is 1. Then call `releaseFirstBatch()` and await the result. Keep the existing assertions after that.

Before releasing that first call, verify spy.mock.calls.length is 1; then release it, await the result, and retain the existing assertions to ensure the test detects overlapping batch calls. ```
--- `91-93`: ** Trivial** · **Maintainability & Code Quality** · **Quick win** **Add a multi-batch test that asserts the summed billed quantity.** The split test returns embeddings without `billableCharacterCount`, so it does not check billed usage. The existing usage test covers one response only. If the adapter kept only the last batch's count, both tests would still pass. The suggested test sends 101 inputs as two batches and expects a billed quantity of 307.
Suggested test
```diff expect(result.embeddings.map((e) => e.vector[0])).toEqual( input.map((_, i) => i), ) }) + it('sums billable characters across batches', async () => { + const adapter = new TestGeminiEmbeddingAdapter( + { apiKey: 'test' }, + 'gemini-embedding-001', + ) + const spy = adapter.spyOnEmbedContent() + spy + .mockResolvedValueOnce({ + embeddings: Array.from({ length: 100 }, () => ({ values: [0.1] })), + metadata: { billableCharacterCount: 300 }, + }) + .mockResolvedValueOnce({ + embeddings: [{ values: [0.2] }], + metadata: { billableCharacterCount: 7 }, + }) + + const input = Array.from({ length: 101 }, (_, i) => `t${i}`) + const result = await adapter.createEmbeddings({ + model: 'gemini-embedding-001', + input, + logger: testLogger, + }) + + expect(result.usage?.billed).toEqual({ + quantity: 307, + unit: 'characters', + }) + }) + it('maps the top-level dimensions option to outputDimensionality', async () => { ```
